column1: # Requirements for Mica::Decimal128, Mica::Currency and Mica::Money (relay
# chunk G5): the API contract of bignum/G5/CONTRACT.md, one line per

column3: .new(coefficient, scale) and .new(Int) accept up to 38 digits and a scale of 0 to 38; more digits raise OverflowError, another scale ArgumentError
parse accepts an optional sign, digits, an optional fraction and an optional exponent, keeps trailing fraction zeros as scale, and reads PostgreSQL and MySQL text
Exponent forms parse to their exact value when it fits 38 digits and scale 38
Malformed text raises ParseError, out-of-range text OverflowError; parse? returns nil for both
to_s writes plain digits with the scale kept and never an exponent
+ and - are exact at the larger scale and raise OverflowError past 38 digits
* is exact at the sum of the scales and raises OverflowError past 38 digits or scale 38
divide rounds to the given scale with the given mode; a zero divisor raises DivisionByZeroError and an oversized quotient OverflowError
TiesAway, TiesEven, Floor, Ceiling, Truncate and Unnecessary act as named on positive and negative ties and non-ties
round lowers the scale with a mode and leaves a value already at or below the scale unchanged
rescale raises the scale exactly and lowers it with a mode, by default Unnecessary
Comparison, equality and hash are by value: 12.30 == 12.3 with equal hashes
to_i64, to_f64, zero?, negative?, abs, unary minus and precision
38-digit coefficients and scale 38 work at the boundary and fail one past it
ParseError, OverflowError, DivisionByZeroError and InexactError descend from Decimal128::Error < Exception
Arithmetic, comparison, hashing, rounding and rescaling allocate nothing
to_json writes a JSON string; from_json reads a string, integer or float token from its text
to_yaml writes the plain scalar and from_yaml reads it back with its scale
to_big_d and Decimal128.new(BigDecimal) convert exactly
The table holds every current ISO 4217 code with its numeric code and minor units (USD 2, JPY 0, BHD 3)
find returns a currency or raises Currency::UnknownError; find? returns nil
Money.new takes a Decimal128, String or Int amount and a Currency or String code
+ and - work between equal currencies and raise CurrencyMismatchError otherwise
* by a Decimal128 or Int is exact
round goes to the currency minor units with the given mode
allocate never loses or invents a minor unit and requires an amount at the minor units (else InexactError)
split of 100.00 USD into 3 is 33.34, 33.33, 33.33; JPY and BHD split at 0 and 3 places
to_s writes the plain amount and the code: 12.30 USD
== and hash are by amount value and currency
